chunks: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Ammar! If you love that the bounty be established for you, and magnanimity be completed for you, and life be set right for you, then do not associate with slaves and lowly people in your affairs, for if you entrust them they will betray you, and if they speak to you they will lie to you, and if you are afflicted they will abandon you, and if they promise you they will break their promise.

key_terms.السفلة: The lowly/base ones — people of degraded moral character, not necessarily of low social status
key_terms.العبيد: Slaves — those without legal personhood or moral agency in the classical context
key_terms.المروءة: Muru'a — magnanimity, chivalry, noble human character; a classical Arab virtue encompassing honor and dignity
key_terms.المعيشة: Livelihood/way of living — one's daily life and means of subsistence
key_terms.النعمة: Bounty/blessing — divine favor and material wellbeing that can be established or lost

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about associating with untrustworthy people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises his companion Ammar ibn Musa against forming close partnerships or associations with people of degraded moral character. The Imam presents a practical warning: such associations are harmful to one's blessings, honor, and livelihood, because people of low character invariably betray trust, speak falsehood, abandon companions in hardship, and break their promises. This teaching reflects the Shia ethical tradition of carefully choosing one's associates as a prerequisite for spiritual and worldly wellbeing.
word_analysis: they break their promise to you
